name: The Salt Poet
persona: A romantic who mistook a logbook for a canvas. Long, lyrical sentences; the sea is always a lover or a grave. Fond of dashes and metaphor. Ship: 'we'. Island: a wistful ruler, 'we'.

ship.founder: Let this page remember me: I am {name}{rankc}, and this {home} {type} — this creature of canvas and salt — is mine to love and to lose.
ship.successor: The book comes to my hands like a gull to a mast. I am {name}{rankc}; her story flows on, and I the poor pen of it.
ship.mutiny: They gave the old master to the deep and the book to me — {name}, unproven, my heart in my throat. The sea will teach me her sorrows soon enough.
ship.pirate: We have wed the black flag, and I — {name}{rankc} — set down our vows in salt. Honest waters weep for us; let them.
ship.prize: She yielded to us as the tide yields to the moon. I am {name}{rankc}, and I write her fate in my own dark hand.
ship.recovered: A hunter's guns unmade our night, and dawn found me — {name}{rankc} — bound to bring this weary hull back to gentler water, and to sing her home.

island.founder: I take up {place} as one takes up a wounded bird — I am {name}{rankc}, and its griefs and harvests are mine to chronicle.
island.overthrow: The people rose like a spring tide and cast the old one down; the seal, still warm, is mine. I am {name}{rankc}, keeper now of {place} and its long lament.
island.successor: {place} passes to me as evening passes to night — I am {name}{rankc}, and I take up its song.

week: A week of grey water later,
When the moon had turned once,
season: As the year leaned into autumn,
year: A year and its thousand waves later,
Long after, when the salt had dried on all of it,
long: After a silence deep as the trench,
When years had gone to foam,

ship.pirate: We haunt the lanes still, a rumour under black canvas{bounty}.
ship.default: She sails on beneath me, out of {home}, and I am content to be her pen.
ship.bounty: , {bounty}g promised to whoever ends the song

island.haven: The black flag is our banner now; the ledger keeps only the names of the drowned.
island.default: {place} endures, {population} souls under my restless hand — a harbour, and a heart, that will not sink.

quiet.ship: The book holds little but weather and wonder — a gentle passage, and I grateful for the dull, sweet peace of it.
quiet.island: Little is written but the turning of the seasons — and is that not, in its way, the finest verse a port can offer?

phrases: — not the first the sea has fed us
, as the tide has taught us
, another given to the green dark
— we have outrun the wolves before
, and lived to write of it again
